Requirements: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree or its equivalent from a college or university of recognized standing. They must also have a strong background in engineering, mathematics, and physics. Required application materials include: a completed application for admission, including statement of purpose, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. A resume or C.V. is also required.
Description:
The graduate field of aerospace engineering provides a program of instruction and research in the disciplines of fluid dynamics, materials and structures, and dynamics and control, with applications to the host of engineering problems that involve the flight of vehicles in the Earth’s atmosphere and in space.

Current research projects are in such areas as computational fluid dynamics; turbulent flows and their control; space vehicle dynamics; combustion; theoretical and applied mechanics of solids and fluids; advanced composite materials; and aeroacoustics. There is close cooperation between the faculty of aerospace engineering and those in related fields, especially mechanical engineering, theoretical and applied mechanics, and electrical and computer engineering.

Students who earn a Ph.D. in aerospace engineering are prepared for leadership roles at the nation’s foremost industrial and government laboratories and as faculty members in university research and teaching.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships (TAs), or Graduate Research Assistantships (GRAs)

Requirements: M.S. or B.S. in engineering, computer science, or a related field. Strong academic record. All applicants must provide a transcript from each college or university attended.
Department: Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
Description:
Robotics is an interdisciplinary field that brings together computer science and engineering to create and study intelligent machines that can perceive and act in the physical world. A Ph.D. in robotics will give you the skills to create the next generation of robotics solutions to the challenges facing our world, from autonomous vehicles and exploration to manufacturing and healthcare.

The graduate field of robotics at Cornell is an interdisciplinary group of researchers working on all aspects of robotics, including perception, control, learning, planning, and human-robot interaction. Faculty and students come from many departments, including computer science, mechanical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, and aerospace engineering. A primary goal of the field is to create an environment where students can focus on robotics research, guided by faculty who are experts in robotics, in a way that is not possible within a traditional departmental structure.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding package including stipend, tuition, and health insurance.
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of admitted Ph.D. students receive full funding.

Requirements: All applicants must submit the following items with their application: statement of purpose; CV or résumé; academic transcripts; three letters of recommendation; writing sample (15-20 pages); English Language Proficiency Requirement - for applicants whose native language is not English.
Concentration: ['African Studies', 'African-American Studies', 'Caribbean Studies']
Description:
The graduate field of Africana studies at Cornell has a long and distinguished history. For over forty years, the faculty has trained students who have become leading scholars in the field. The Ph.D. program in Africana studies is interdisciplinary. It aims to provide students with a firm foundation in the contested history of the field, its seminal texts, and its key concepts, theories and methods. Students will develop an understanding of the scholarly and social-movement origins of Africana studies, as well as the relationships among its diverse intellectual and political traditions. Students will also be expected to achieve depth in a specific area or topic related to the study of the African diaspora.

The field has two required courses, one in theory and method and the other in history of the field. Students can specialize in African, African-American or Caribbean studies. They also can take advantage of faculty specializations in areas such as Africana feminisms, expressive arts and literature, history, and political economy and development.

Students applying to this field are admitted to the Ph.D. program. The field does not admit students for a terminal M.A. degree.
ScholarshipType: All students admitted to the Ph.D. program are offered a multi-year funding package, which includes a stipend, full tuition, and health insurance.

ProgramName: (M.P.S.) in Agriculture and Life Sciences (Biological and Environmental Engineering)
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Biological and Environmental Engineering
Description:
The Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Agriculture and Life Sciences is a one-year, course-based master’s degree that prepares individuals for the workplace. The M.P.S. degree is for individuals who are interested in in-depth study in a particular academic field, but who do not wish to pursue a traditional, research-based Ph.D. The degree has a strong foundation in a specific sub-discipline, combined with structured professional development coursework and a problem-solving project instead of a thesis. The M.P.S. degree program is designed to be completed in two semesters of full-time study.

Students in the graduate field of biological and environmental engineering are part of an interdisciplinary group that applies basic sciences and engineering to living systems and the environment. Students can specialize in a variety of areas, such as bioprocess engineering, bioenvironmental engineering, sustainable energy systems, industrial biotechnology, synthetic biology, ecosystem and water-resources engineering, engineering for a circular economy, digital agriculture, waste treatment and management, soil and water bio-geochemistry and environmental management.

ProgramName: (minor) in American Indian and Indigenous Studies
Description: The graduate minor in American Indian and Indigenous Studies (AIIS) provides an opportunity for students to engage in the interdisciplinary study of Native American societies and cultures. The graduate minor is open to all Cornell graduate students. The program works closely with students to craft a curriculum that both complements their disciplinary interests and expands their knowledge of Indigenous issues. Coursework must be taken with at least two faculty members of the AIIS graduate field who represent at least two different fields of study. The director of graduate studies (DGS) serves as the minor field member on the student’s special committee. Students pursuing the AIIS minor will be part of a vibrant intellectual community that includes faculty and students from a variety of disciplines and national backgrounds. They will receive regular invitations to lectures, workshops, and other events that address a wide range of topics related to American Indian and Indigenous Studies.

Requirements: The American Studies Program at Cornell University offers a graduate minor for students who are enrolled in a doctoral program in any field at the University. A student who wishes to minor in American Studies should first consult the Director of Graduate Studies (DGS) for American Studies, who will assist the student in selecting a minor member for his or her special committee. No formal application is required.
Description: The graduate minor in American Studies offers students an opportunity to participate in a field defined by its interdisciplinary and transnational scope and its critical attention to historical and contemporary formations of race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, class, and empire. In both their coursework and their own research, students in the minor draw on a range of approaches—including literary and visual analysis, ethnography, and archival research—to explore the territory between and across traditional disciplines. The director of graduate studies (DGS) works with each student to devise a course of study that best complements the student’s work in their major field.

Requirements: All applicants must submit a statement of purpose, transcripts, and two letters of recommendation. GRE test scores are not required and will not be accepted or reviewed by the admission committee if submitted.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: ['Animal Nutrition', 'Animal Physiology and Reproduction', 'Breeding and Genetics', 'Dairy Cattle Management', 'Livestock, Poultry and Companion Animal Biology']
Description: The M.P.S. in animal science is an intensive, one-year, non-thesis master’s program designed for individuals who need more academic preparation for professional school (veterinary, medical, dental), or who wish to expand their knowledge of a specific area of animal science before entering the workforce. M.P.S. students choose a concentration area and, guided by a faculty advisor, take courses from across the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and the university to develop an individualized program. The M.P.S. degree culminates with a capstone project which applies academic knowledge to solve a real-world problem.

Requirements: An undergraduate degree in animal science is not required, but applicants are expected to have a strong background in the basic biological and physical sciences. Recommended courses include general biology and chemistry, organic chemistry, biochemistry, genetics, and calculus. Courses in nutrition, physiology, and microbiology are also desirable. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is strongly recommended.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Animal Breeding and Genetics, Animal and Data Science, Animal Nutrition, Animal Physiology
Description: The graduate field of animal science offers M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs with a concentration in one of the following areas: animal breeding and genetics; animal nutrition; animal physiology; or animal and data science. Course work is designed to give the student a strong background in the basic sciences and in the specialized area of concentration. Students are expected to complete an original research project that contributes new knowledge to the field of animal science. Each student's program is designed by the student and his or her Special Committee.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: ['animal breeding and genetics', 'animal nutrition', 'animal physiology', 'animal management']
Description: The graduate field of animal science offers M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs with a concentration in one of the following animal sciences: animal breeding and genetics, animal nutrition, animal physiology, or animal management. Within these concentrations, students have a wide range of topic areas from which to choose. For example, animal nutrition includes biochemical, molecular, and applied aspects of the nutrition of a variety of animal species. Animal physiology includes reproductive, lactation, and growth physiology.
AverageScholarshipAmount: The standard 9-month stipend rate for 2024-2025 is $43,982.
ScholarshipAmount: All Ph.D. students receive a full funding package that includes a stipend, full tuition coverage, and health insurance. The standard 9-month stipend rate for 2024-2025 is $43,982.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Animal Science
Description:
The graduate field of animal science offers M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs with a concentration in animal science. In this research-based degree program, students work with one of Cornell’s world-class faculty members and have access to state-of-the-art research facilities. Research programs in animal science apply basic and applied sciences to the study of the biology and management of domestic animals, including livestock, companion, and laboratory animals. Specific areas of research include animal genetics and genomics, animal nutrition, animal physiology, and animal welfare and management. The goal of these research programs is to improve animal productivity, health, and well-being.

Most students pursuing an M.S. or Ph.D. in animal science focus their research within one of four general areas: animal breeding and genetics, animal nutrition, animal physiology, or animal welfare and management. Research in animal breeding and genetics covers quantitative, molecular, and computational genetics and genomics and aims to improve the health and productivity of both domestic and non-domesticated species of animals. Research in animal nutrition focuses on the digestion, absorption, metabolism, and excretion of nutrients in order to improve nutrient utilization and efficiency, improve animal health, and reduce the environmental impact of animal agriculture. Research in physiology is aimed at understanding the basic biology of animals with a particular emphasis on the biology of reproduction, lactation, growth, and development. Research in animal management and welfare examines the effects of management and housing systems on animal health, well-being, and productivity, and aims to develop more sustainable animal production systems. Research in all of these areas is conducted at the whole animal, organ system, cellular, and molecular levels. Students are not restricted to one of these areas of study and can take a multi-disciplinary approach by including faculty from other areas of animal science and other graduate fields as part of their special committee.

In addition to the graduate field of animal science, other graduate fields that may be of interest to students include biomedical and biological sciences, food science and technology, and zoology and wildlife conservation.

Requirements: All applicants must submit a complete online application. Your statement of purpose should be no longer than two single-spaced pages. Three letters of recommendation are required. A writing sample is required. It should demonstrate your capacity for graduate-level work and should relate to your proposed research interests. It may be a paper written for a class, a chapter from an honors or M.A. thesis, or a professional publication. The sample should be no longer than 35 pages (double spaced, excluding bibliography). A CV/résumé is required.
Description: Anthropology is the comparative study of humankind, from its beginnings millions of years ago to the present day. The field of anthropology at Cornell is composed of three subfields: sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, and biological anthropology. Sociocultural anthropology is the study of contemporary human societies and cultures. Archaeology is the study of past human societies and cultures through the material remains they have left behind. Biological anthropology is the study of human and non-human primate evolution and adaptation, past and present. The graduate program is designed to provide the institutional setting, financial support, and intellectual community for developing professional competence in one of these three subfields. We encourage research that is theoretically engaged, ethnographically grounded, and interdisciplinary in nature. The program offers a Ph.D. in anthropology. Although the M.A. is not a terminal degree, students admitted to the Ph.D. program may receive an M.A. after fulfilling certain requirements.
ScholarshipAmount: $34,068/9-months (minimum stipend)
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, teaching assistantships, and/or research assistantships

Department: Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management
Concentration: Environmental, Energy, and Resource Economics, Food and Agricultural Economics, Management
Description:
The graduate field of applied economics and management (AEM) offers two master's degrees and a Ph.D. The field houses a large, diverse, and distinguished faculty with a wide array of research and outreach programs focusing on three subject matter areas:

Environmental, energy and resource economics (EERE)
Food and agricultural economics (FAE)
Management (MGT)

The master of science (M.S.) degree is a two-year academic program focusing on the development of research skills and the completion of a master's thesis in one of the three subject matter areas. Students receiving this degree are prepared to enter a Ph.D. program or to work in an applied research position in the public or private sectors. Students entering the M.S. degree program receive a generous funding package that covers tuition and provides a stipend.

The master of professional studies (M.P.S.) degree is a one-year professional degree for students with an undergraduate degree and professional experience who are interested in enhancing their knowledge of one of the subject matter areas. A variety of concentrations are offered in each of the subject matter areas. Students have considerable flexibility in the choice of courses and are required to complete a problem-solving project advised by a faculty member.

The doctor of philosophy (Ph.D.) degree trains students for careers in research and teaching. Graduates take positions at leading academic institutions, international research centers, government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and private-sector firms. Ph.D. students work closely with AEM faculty members and often collaborate with faculty and graduate students from other fields at Cornell, such as economics, management, natural resources, policy analysis and management, and civil engineering.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and the SC Johnson College of Business
Concentration: Environmental, Energy, and Resource Economics; Food and Agricultural Economics; International and Development Economics; Management; Behavioral Economics
Description: The Ph.D. program in Applied Economics and Management (AEM) prepares students for careers as professional economists in academia, government, or the private sector. The distinguishing feature of the AEM Ph.D. program is its focus on applying the theories and methods of economics to today’s real-world problems. The coursework and research of our graduate students reflects this emphasis on applied work.
ScholarshipType: Full funding package including a full tuition waiver, a nine-month stipend, and student health insurance.

Requirements:
All applicants must submit a complete application including a statement of purpose, resume, and three letters of recommendation. GRE general test scores are NOT required.

The field does not have a minimum GPA requirement, but most accepted students have a GPA of 3.5 or higher.
Department: Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science
Concentration: Information Technology, User Experience (UX) Design, Data Science & Analytics
Description:
The master of professional studies (M.P.S.) in applied information science (AIS) is a one-year, course-based master’s degree that provides students with the knowledge and skills to succeed in careers that require a deep understanding of information science and technology. The program prepares students for a variety of careers including data scientists, UX designers, product managers, technology analysts, and more.

The MPS in AIT degree program has three tracks: Information Technology, User Experience (UX) Design, and Data Science & Analytics. The curriculum is flexible, with options for students to tailor their course of study to their own interests and career goals. Students take a combination of foundational courses, specialized electives, and a capstone project. In the project, students work in teams to solve a real-world problem for a client, giving them hands-on experience and the opportunity to apply their skills in a professional setting. The program is designed for students from a variety of backgrounds, including those with degrees in computer science, engineering, business, and the humanities. We also welcome students with professional experience who are looking to transition into a new career or advance in their current one.

Concentration: ['Applied Mathematics', 'Operations Research']
Description: The graduate field of applied mathematics offers a Ph.D. and a terminal M.S. degree. Students in the Ph.D. program can pursue a concentration in either applied mathematics or operations research. The Ph.D. program is flexible and is designed to accommodate a variety of student interests. It is a research-oriented degree, and all students write a dissertation. The M.S. is a two-semester professional degree. A specific curriculum of courses provides students with a strong base in the techniques and theory of applied mathematics and operations research. This program provides excellent training for a variety of industrial and government positions. Applied mathematics is an interdisciplinary field that focuses on the creation and imaginative use of mathematical concepts to pose and solve problems over the entire gamut of the physical, biological, and social sciences, in engineering, and in finance. It is a dynamic field, which is constantly developing new mathematical tools in response to new problems and which finds new areas of application for existing mathematics. The Cornell Center for Applied Mathematics, which administers the graduate field, has 10 core faculty members and over 80 associated faculty members from 16 departments. These faculty members bring an enormous breadth and depth to the applied mathematics program. Their interests include—but are not restricted to—the areas of applied analysis, computational mathematics, dynamical systems, fluid dynamics, industrial and engineering mathematics, mathematical biology, mathematical finance, mechanics, networks, optimization, probability, and statistics.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding, including tuition, stipend, and health insurance.

Department: School of Applied and Engineering Physics in the College of Engineering
Concentration: ['solid-state physics', 'quantum and nonlinear optics', 'condensed-matter physics', 'biophysics', 'advanced materials and nanotechnology', 'plasma physics', 'synchrotron radiation-based research', 'novel accelerator technology']
Description: The Field of Applied Physics offers a Ph.D. and a terminal M.S. degree. This field is appropriate for students who wish to pursue research in an area of applied physics. Because applied physics is interdisciplinary, graduate students have the flexibility to create a course of study that is matched to their specific research interests. The field faculty are drawn from ten Cornell departments, which provides students with a wide range of research choices.

Requirements: An undergraduate degree in physics, engineering physics, or a related discipline is required. Research experience is desirable but not required. All applicants must provide the following items with their application: an academic statement of purpose, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation.
Department: School of Applied and Engineering Physics
Concentration: Condensed-matter and materials physics, quantum information and quantum matter, optics and photonics, biophysics, and plasma physics
Description: Applied Physics at Cornell is a field characterized by the application of physical principles to a variety of problems in engineering and science. The curriculum is flexible and can be adapted to individual interests. The field is composed of faculty from several departments in the College of Engineering and the College of Arts and Sciences. Research concentrations include: condensed-matter and materials physics, quantum information and quantum matter, optics and photonics, biophysics, and plasma physics. Many research projects are carried out in collaboration with the excellent interdisciplinary research centers at Cornell. Students entering the Ph.D. program should have a strong preparation in physics or a related discipline with a solid background in mathematics. Typically, during the first year of graduate study, students concentrate on their coursework and serve as teaching assistants. By the end of the first year, students usually select a thesis advisor and a research area. During the second year, coursework is generally completed, and students begin their thesis research. A qualifying examination for the Ph.D. is usually taken at the end of the second year. Students with an appropriate undergraduate degree can enter the Ph.D. program directly.

Requirements: All applicants must submit a statement of purpose, a writing sample, and three letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Aegean, Anatolian, and Cypriot Prehistory and History, Archaeological Science, Classical Archaeology, Egyptology and Near Eastern Archaeology, European Archaeology, Mesoamerican Archaeology, North American Archaeology, South American Archaeology, South Asian Archaeology, Southeast Asian Archaeology
Description: Archaeology at Cornell is an interdisciplinary program, drawing faculty and students from a variety of departments in the humanities and social sciences. The Program of Archaeology is not a degree-granting department; rather, faculty members in the program belong to other departments at Cornell. Graduate students are admitted to the Graduate School through the graduate field of archaeology, and they work toward a M.A. or a Ph.D. degree in archaeology. Graduate students admitted to the program must focus on a specific area of study that is well represented by the faculty. Cornell has particular strengths in the archaeology of the following areas: the Aegean, the ancient Near East, classical Greece and Rome, Egypt, Europe, North America, Mesoamerica, South America, and South and Southeast Asia. Students should consult the list of faculty to identify those with whom they might work. Topical strengths of the program include but are not limited to archaeobotany, archaeometallurgy, bioarchaeology, ceramic analysis, dendrochronology, geoarchaeology, heritage studies, household archaeology, lithic analysis, and zooarchaeology. Graduate students must secure a commitment from at least one archaeology faculty member to serve on their special committee before they will be considered for admission to the program. The director of graduate studies in archaeology is able to help prospective students in this process. Contact information for the director of graduate studies in archaeology may be found under Contact Information on the right side of this page. Cornell has an extensive system of libraries, with holdings relevant to all areas of archaeological inquiry. The program is affiliated with the Cornell Institute of Archaeology and Material Studies (CIAMS) which provides a network for archaeological research and teaching across the university. CIAMS hosts a lecture series and a variety of workshops. It also offers support for student research and conference travel.

Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Concentration: ['Computer Graphics', 'Matter Design Computation', 'Sustainable Building Systems']
Description: The graduate field of Architectural Science offers a post-professional Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Architectural Science. This research-based degree program prepares students for careers in academia, industry, and specialized consulting. The program offers three main concentrations: Computer Graphics, Matter Design Computation, and Sustainable Building Systems. The degree path for each concentration is developed through a custom curriculum consisting of required and elective courses and a final thesis. Coursework and research are highly interdisciplinary with opportunities to work with faculty from various departments across the university. The M.S. degree in Architectural Science is a two-year STEM-designated degree program.

ProgramName: (M.S.) in Architectural Science - Matter Design Computation
Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Concentration: Matter Design Computation
Description:
The Master of Science in Architectural Science is a post-professional research-based degree program with a concentration in Matter Design Computation. The program operates at the intersection of architecture, computation, engineering, and material science, and offers a framework for research as a focused and in-depth academic endeavor. The curriculum provides a solid intellectual basis for advanced and independent research, along with the development of the necessary skills for in-depth technical investigations into emerging material technologies.

The degree program is intended for applicants who hold a professional degree in architecture or related fields, and who are interested in engaging in advanced research. Matter Design Computation focuses on materials, with an emphasis on research informed by the latest manufacturing technologies and computational design techniques. A central concern is the development of innovative design and fabrication strategies for novel performative material systems in the context of architecture. This program provides students with the opportunity to pursue individualized research under the guidance of our internationally recognized faculty. The M.S. degree in Architectural Science is intended to be a terminal degree. Upon its successful completion, graduates are qualified to continue on to a Ph.D. degree or to enter the profession as specialists in practice.

ProgramName: (Ph.D.) in History of Architecture and Urban Development
Requirements: All applicants must submit a statement of purpose, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. GRE general test is not required. International applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency. A TOEFL or IELTS test is required for applicants whose native language is not English. Applicants should also submit a writing sample. For additional information, please visit the History of Architecture and Urban Development Ph.D. website.
Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Description: The graduate field of the History of Architecture and Urban Development (HAUD) is a Ph.D. program offered by the Department of the History of Architecture and Urbanism in the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. The program focuses on the history, theory, and criticism of architecture, landscape, and urban design from antiquity to the present. The program is committed to a diversity of historical approaches. HAUD has particular strengths in early modern, modern, and contemporary architecture and urbanism in a global context, with specializations in Asia, Africa, Europe, and North and Latin America. The program takes advantage of Cornell’s interdisciplinary resources, encouraging students to make connections with other fields in the humanities. HAUD prepares students for careers in research and teaching in universities, for curatorial positions in museums and archives, and for careers in architectural criticism and journalism.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships (TAs), Graduate Research Assistantships (GRAs), and Research Assistantships (RAs)

Requirements:
The application and all supporting documents must be submitted online. Applicants are expected to have a good grounding in an Asian language appropriate to their proposed field of study. Please indicate your proposed major and minor concentrations on the application form. You are welcome to contact a faculty member in your chosen concentration before applying.

Application requirements:

A Statement of Purpose is required.
A writing sample is required. It should be no more than 20 pages.
Three letters of recommendation are required.
The GRE general test is not required and scores will not be accepted or reviewed by the admissions committee if submitted.
Transcripts are required from each college or university you have attended.
The English Language Proficiency Requirement for all applicants.
Concentration: ['East Asia', 'South Asia', 'Southeast Asia']
Description:
The graduate field of Asian Studies includes the study of the languages and cultures of East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. The field is structured to provide an unparalleled opportunity for graduate students to design a course of study that is at once broad in its attention to Asia as a whole, focused in its concentration on a particular country or region, and grounded in a disciplinary approach.

The field is structured into three distinct geographical concentrations: East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Within these concentrations, students select a major country or area of specialization. In consultation with their Special Committees, students will also select a major discipline on which their programs will be focused and one or two minor disciplines that will complement their major disciplinary focus.
ScholarshipAmount: Guaranteed funding package includes a minimum $43,100 stipend (9-month), full tuition coverage, and health insurance for five years.

Requirements:
All applicants must submit the following items with their application:

*   Statement of purpose
*   Résumé or curriculum vitae
*   Three letters of recommendation
*   Transcripts
*   English Language Proficiency Requirement – For applicants whose native language is not English, the TOEFL or IELTS test is required. See the Graduate School’s English Language Proficiency Requirement for more information.
*   GRE Scores – The GRE general test is not required. The GRE physics subject test is recommended, but not required. If you have already taken the general GRE and would like to inlude it in your application, you may. Please send scores to the Cornell University Graduate School, institution code 2098. No department code is needed.
Concentration: Astronomy, Planetary Science, Space Sciences and Engineering
Description: The graduate field of Astronomy and Space Sciences covers a wide range of subjects, including theoretical and observational astrophysics, general relativity and cosmology, planetary science, and the development of instrumentation for ground-based and space-borne observatories. It includes faculty members not only from the Department of Astronomy but also from a number of cooperating departments, principally Physics and Electrical and Computer Engineering. Students may specialize in any of these areas. The field offers a range of specializations, from the purely theoretical to the strictly observational, as well as to spacecraft and instrumentation.

Requirements:
All applicants must provide a transcript from each college or university attended.
Statement of Purpose is required. The statement of purpose is expected to be approximately 1-2 pages in length and is a very important part of the application.
Three letters of recommendation are required.
The GRE General Test is not accepted.
For applicants whose native language is not English, the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) is required. We require a minimum TOEFL iBT score of 105. We do not accept the “MyBest” TOEFL scores. Within the iBT, we require minimum sub-scores of Writing: 20, Listening: 15, Reading: 20, Speaking: 22. The TOEFL may be waived if the applicant meets the requirements for an exception.
Concentration: ['General Astronomy', 'General Space Sciences', 'Planetary Science', 'Physical Sciences']
Description: The graduate field of astronomy and space sciences offers a broad range of research opportunities in a similarly broad range of research areas: astrophysics; cosmology and relativity; planetary science; and space sciences. Students are admitted to the Ph.D. program through the graduate field. The M.S. degree is generally awarded as a transitional degree for Ph.D. students after two years of study and upon completion of the A-exam.
ScholarshipAmount: Full financial support which includes a stipend, full tuition, and health insurance.
ScholarshipType: fellowship, a research assistantship, or a teaching assistantship

Requirements: All applicants must submit a complete application including a statement of purpose, transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, at least three letters of recommendation, and a Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume. GRE test scores are optional. Applicants are expected to have a strong background in a quantitative science such as physics, chemistry, engineering, or mathematics. Preparation should include three semesters of calculus, differential equations, and a year of calculus-based physics. Some background in chemistry and computer programming is also desirable. Students lacking some of the desired preparation may be admitted, but will be expected to make up the deficiencies early in their graduate study.
Department: College of Engineering and College of Arts and Sciences
Description: Atmospheric science is an interdisciplinary field that applies principles of physics, chemistry, and mathematics to the study of the atmosphere. The graduate field of atmospheric sciences at Cornell offers students a wide variety of research opportunities in a broad range of topics, including climate dynamics and climate change, atmospheric chemistry and biogeochemistry, cloud physics, and atmospheric boundary-layer processes. The field works closely with the Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences and is composed of faculty from various departments and centers at Cornell, including the departments of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Biological and Environmental Engineering, Civil and Environmental Engineering, and Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. This interdisciplinary character of the field provides an opportunity for students to acquire a broad understanding of the atmospheric sciences, a deep knowledge in a particular area of specialization, and an appreciation for the interconnections among different areas of the field.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Research Assistantships

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and College of Engineering
Description:
The graduate field of atmospheric sciences at Cornell is an interdisciplinary program with faculty from four departments in three different colleges. This structure reflects the interdisciplinary nature of the field itself, which covers a wide range of subjects, from the fundamental physics and chemistry of the atmosphere and ocean, to the development of instrumentation and large-scale computational models. The program offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in atmospheric sciences. The field also offers an accelerated M.S. degree option for qualifying Cornell undergraduate majors.

The M.S. degree requires coursework with a concentration in some area of atmospheric sciences, the completion of a research project, and writing and defense of a thesis. The Ph.D. degree requires coursework, passing a qualifying examination (the “A Exam”), completion of a significant and original research project, and the writing and defense of a dissertation (the “B Exam”). For both degrees, each student, with the help of a Special Committee, develops a course of study and research appropriate to his or her background and interests.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition, a stipend, and health insurance are guaranteed for all Ph.D. students in good academic standing.
ScholarshipType: Teaching assistantships (TAs), research assistantships (RAs), fellowships, and graduate assistantships (GAs)

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and College of Engineering
Concentration: ['Atmosphere-ocean/climate dynamics and climate change', 'Atmospheric chemistry and biogeochemistry', 'Atmospheric physics, including meteorology, boundary-layer processes, and cloud physics']
Description: The graduate field of Atmospheric Sciences offers students a program of study in the science of the atmosphere, leading to the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees. Research is conducted in many areas of atmospheric sciences, including atmospheric dynamics and weather, climate, atmospheric chemistry, and atmospheric physics. The field has three major areas of focus: atmosphere-ocean/climate dynamics and climate change; atmospheric chemistry and biogeochemistry; and atmospheric physics, including meteorology, boundary-layer processes, and cloud physics. Students work on specific projects with their Special Committee chair from the graduate field of Atmospheric Sciences, which has faculty in the department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, as well as faculty members in the department of Biological and Environmental Engineering. There are excellent opportunities for interdisciplinary studies at Cornell, for example, with faculty members in the fields of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Computational Science and Engineering, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Astronomy, as well as other departments such as Applied and Engineering Physics and the various engineering schools.

Department: College of Human Ecology and College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Community Nutrition
Description:
The graduate field of Nutrition provides students with a strong foundation in basic and applied nutritional sciences through course work and original research in an environment of multidisciplinary collaboration. The field comprises more than 40 faculty members from 11 departments and 4 colleges, with interests spanning from the level of the molecule to that of the population. Concentrations for the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees are offered in: Molecular Nutrition, Human Nutrition, Community Nutrition, and International Nutrition.

Molecular Nutrition: This concentration focuses on the metabolic and biochemical basis of nutrition. Students in this concentration integrate the principles of genetics, biochemistry, physiology, and nutrition to understand the role of nutrients in gene expression, cell signaling, and metabolism. Research areas include nutrient-gene interactions, nutrient signaling, vitamin and mineral metabolism, nutrient bioavailability, lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, and amino acid metabolism.

Human Nutrition: This concentration emphasizes the integration of human metabolism and nutritional biochemistry. Students in this concentration gain in-depth knowledge of how nutrients and dietary patterns influence human health and disease. Research may be conducted with human subjects or in clinical settings.

Community Nutrition: This concentration focuses on human nutrition as it relates to promoting health and preventing disease in communities. Students in this concentration may focus on behavioral nutrition, nutrition intervention and policy, or epidemiology. Coursework covers nutritional sciences, statistics, human development, sociology, communication, and economics.

International Nutrition: This concentration emphasizes the nutritional problems of developing countries. Students in this concentration focus on the causes and consequences of malnutrition, and the design and evaluation of nutrition interventions at the individual, household, community, national and international levels. A unique aspect of this concentration is the summer field experience.

A unique feature of graduate study in Nutrition at Cornell is the opportunity for students to tailor their programs to their specific interests by taking courses and working with faculty in a wide range of disciplines.

ProgramName: (M.S.) in Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Arts and Sciences, College of Engineering, College of Veterinary Medicine
Concentration: Biochemistry and Structural Biology, Biophysics, Cell and Developmental Biology, Chemical Biology, Computational Biology, Genetics, Genomics, and Development, Molecular and Cellular Physiology, Proteomics and Metabolomics, Systems Biology
Description: The graduate field of Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology (BMCB) is an intercollege field consisting of faculty from the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, the College of Arts and Sciences, the College of Veterinary Medicine, the College of Engineering, and the Boyce Thompson Institute. The Field of BMCB provides a training and research environment of the highest caliber for students pursuing a PhD or MS degree. The research interests of the faculty are diverse, spanning all areas of modern molecular life sciences. The Field's greatest strength is in its exceptional training opportunities in the core disciplines of biochemistry, biophysics, cell biology, genetics, and molecular biology. Students learn to become creative and independent scientific investigators by completing original research, which becomes the basis of the PhD dissertation or MS thesis. A PhD or MS degree in BMCB leads to careers in research and/or teaching in academia, industry, or government. The Field also provides an excellent background for careers in a wide variety of other areas, such as law, business, policy, and communications.
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted students receive a full tuition waiver and a stipend ($42,600 for 2024-25).

ProgramName: (Ph.D.) in Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and College of Arts and Sciences
Description: The graduate field of Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology (BMCB) is an intercollege field composed of over 70 faculty members from eight departments in four colleges. The field offers Ph.D. training in the broad area of modern molecular life sciences for students who have a strong background in biology and/or chemistry. Our goal is to train a diverse student body to be creative, independent scientists and leaders in a wide variety of careers. Research in BMCB spans a broad range of topics including biochemistry and structural biology; cell biology; molecular biology; computational biology; developmental biology and genetics; chemical biology; and physical biology. Students have a wide choice of thesis laboratories. The first-year curriculum provides a solid foundation for the pursuit of a Ph.d. degree while emphasizing flexibility to meet the individual needs and interests of the students. The first semester curriculum consists of a one-semester graduate core course in biochemistry, molecular and cell biology; a course in scientific writing and logic; and three laboratory rotations. Coursework during the second semester of the first year and beyond is chosen by the student and their Special Committee from a diverse menu of advanced courses.

Description: The graduate field of biological and environmental engineering offers programs leading to research degrees (M.S. and Ph.D.) and professional degrees (M.Eng. and M.P.S.). M.S. and Ph.D. programs focus on original research, preparing students for leadership in academic, industrial, and government research and development. Professional degree programs focus on design, technical management, and other aspects of professional practice, preparing students for a wide range of career options.

Concentration: ['Bioenergy', 'Bioenvironmental Engineering', 'Bioprocess Engineering', 'Biotechnology', 'Ecological Engineering', 'Environmental Engineering', 'Food Engineering', 'Industrial Biotechnology', 'Nanobiotechnology', 'Soil and Water Engineering', 'Sustainable Energy Systems', 'Synthetic Biology']
Description: Research in biological and environmental engineering links the physical and biological sciences to create knowledge and designs for a wide range of biological and environmental systems. At Cornell, the field is organized into a flexible program with faculty who specialize in a wide range of topics that are grouped into ten concentrations. Students select a research adviser and develop their academic program around one of these topics, or in a cross-disciplinary specialty of their own design in close consultation with their special committee.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Arts and Sciences, College of Engineering, College of Veterinary Medicine
Concentration: Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology, Cancer Biology, Immunology and Infectious Disease, Microbiology, Pharmacology, Physiology, Biophysics, and Systems Biology, Stem Cell Biology
Description:
The graduate field of Biomedical and Biological Sciences (BBS) is an umbrella program for the basic biomedical sciences at Cornell University. First-year BBS students have the opportunity to explore a variety of research areas before selecting a specific field of study and a thesis advisor.

Upon entering the program, students may choose to work with any of more than 160 faculty members in seven major fields of study, based at the College of Veterinary Medicine and the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences. After completing three or four lab rotations in their first year, students select a major field and a mentor. They then complete the Ph.D. degree in that major field.

The seven major fields of study are:
- Biochemistry, Molecular and Cell Biology
- Cancer Biology
- Immunology and Infectious Disease
- Microbiology
- Pharmacology
- Physiology, Biophysics, and Systems Biology
- Stem Cell Biology

The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of modern biomedical science, as well as an in-depth understanding of one or more of the above areas. All students are required to participate in laboratory rotations and teaching. They also participate in journal clubs and seminars. Students may earn a minor in any field offered for graduate study at Cornell. This structure offers a high degree of flexibility that allows students to tailor the program to their individual needs and interests.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Research Assistantships

Department: Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering, College of Engineering
Concentration: ['Biomaterials', 'Biomechanics', 'Biomedical devices and instrumentation', 'Biomedical imaging', 'Drug delivery', 'Systems and synthetic biology', 'Tissue engineering']
Description:
The Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering at Cornell University is a research and education community that is creating the next generation of life-saving medical solutions. In a culture of collaboration, we are training the biomedical engineers of the future and leading research and discovery that will improve human health. The field offers Ph.D., M.S., and M.Eng. degrees.

The one-year M.Eng. degree provides students with advanced training in biomedical engineering to prepare them for careers in industry or further graduate studies. The flexible, coursework-based program features a team-based design project that solves a real-world medical challenge.

Requirements: All Graduate School Requirements, including the TOEFL Exam for non-native English speakers. All GRE test scores optional
Concentration: ['Biomechanics and Mechanobiology', 'Biomedical Imaging and Instrumentation', 'Drug Delivery and Nanomedicine', 'Molecular and Cellular Engineering', 'Systems and Synthetic Biology', 'Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine']
Description:
The graduate field of biomedical engineering at Cornell is a diverse community of researchers and students that is engaged in the most cutting-edge biomedical research at the interface of engineering, biology, and medicine. Cornell BME offers an enriching graduate program that will prepare students for successful and impactful careers in academic research, industrial research and development, and entrepreneurship.

Our M.S. and Ph.D. students take classes across the entire Ithaca campus, including the College of Engineering, College of Veterinary Medicine and Weill Cornell Medicine in New York City.

The M.S. program is a two-year, thesis-based program focused on training students for a future research career. This can lead to a career in academia or industry, and it also prepares students for the Ph.D. program. The program is flexible to accommodate students of diverse backgrounds and varying interests.

Requirements: Application to the Ph.D. program is aimed at students with a bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or in the physical or biological sciences with a strong quantitative background. Applicants must have completed a minimum of one year of calculus, one year of physics, one year of chemistry, and at least one course in biology and one course in computer programming. The most competitive applicants typically have a GPA of 3.5 or higher (on a 4.0 scale), undergraduate research experience, and a clear vision for their graduate research that matches the interests of one or more of our faculty.
Department: Nancy E. and Peter C. Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering
Concentration: ['Biomaterials and Drug Delivery', 'Biomechanics and Mechanobiology', 'Biomedical Imaging and Instrumentation', 'Molecular, Cellular, and Systems Engineering', 'Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine']
Description: The graduate field of biomedical engineering at Cornell is a diverse and interdisciplinary field that offers M.S., Ph.D., and M.Eng. degrees. The mission of the Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering is to educate students to be leaders in biomedical engineering by fostering learning, discovery, and invention in a creative and collaborative environment. The school’s internationally recognized faculty are committed to this mission and to advancing health and well-being through the integration of engineering, life sciences and medicine. The school is housed in Weill Hall, a state-of-the-art facility for life science research. The interdisciplinary research themes of the school include: biomaterials and drug delivery; biomedical imaging and instrumentation; biomechanics and mechanobiology; molecular and cellular engineering; systems and computational biology; and tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding is guaranteed for all Ph.D. students, which includes full tuition, a living stipend (the university minimum rate is $34,064 for 2024-25), and student health insurance.

Requirements: All applicants must provide a statement of purpose and a resume. Three letters of recommendation are required. For the M.S. program, it is required that the applicant have taken, at minimum, two semesters of calculus, a course in matrix algebra, a course in probability, and a course in statistics.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science
Description: The graduate field of biometry and statistics encompasses the theory and application of statistics in the biological and life sciences. The primary objective of the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree programs is to train students to become professional statisticians. The field is composed of faculty from the Department of Biological Statistics and Computational Biology as well as from other departments at Cornell.

Requirements: All applicants must submit the following items with their application: statement of purpose, résumé, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts. Please indicate in your Statement of Purpose which of our faculty members you are most interested in working with and why. A list of faculty can be found here. Please do not contact faculty members directly prior to applying.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and the Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science
Concentration: biometry, statistics, computational biology, and mathematical statistics
Description: Biometry is the application of statistical and mathematical methods to the biological sciences. The field of biometry and statistics at Cornell has graduate students in four concentrations: biometry, statistics, computational biology, and mathematical statistics. Students take courses in the core subjects of mathematical statistics and probability, statistical methods, and linear models. Advanced courses are available in each of the concentration areas. The graduate program is designed to be flexible and to accommodate the interests of each student. There are typically 50 students in residence, almost all of whom are Ph.D. students. All students have financial support and are actively engaged in research with one or more faculty members.

Description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) degree in Chemical Engineering from Cornell is a course-work and project-based program that provides students with a high-level, advanced education in chemical engineering. The program can be completed in as few as nine months, and coursework and project work can be tailored to meet a student’s specific interests. The M.Eng. program is a terminal degree that is not intended for students wishing to pursue a Ph.D. degree at another institution.

The graduate field of Chemical Engineering offers a program of study leading to the research-oriented degrees of Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.), as well as a professional degree, the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.). The M.S. and Ph.D. programs are oriented toward research. The M.Eng. program is a one-year, course-based professional degree program. Students admitted for the M.S. or Ph.D. degrees enroll in the Field of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, and their degree is in Chemical Engineering. The Field has no specific course requirements; each student’s program is planned in consultation with a Special Committee of the graduate faculty chosen by the student. For the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees, the Special Committee must have a minimum of two and three members, respectively. The chairperson of the committee is the student’s research advisor. The other members of the committee, the minor members, must be from outside the Field of Chemical Engineering. This structure gives each student the freedom to design a course of study and a research program that is best suited to his or her own individual interests and needs. Students may choose minor subjects from a wide range of related disciplines, including chemistry and chemical biology, biological and environmental engineering, food science and technology, civil and environmental engineering, materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, theoretical and applied mechanics, electrical engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, and business.

Description: The graduate field of Chemical Engineering offers a doctoral program that is characterized by a flexible, research-oriented curriculum. In consultation with their Special Committee, students design an individualized course of study based on their specific research interests and career goals. Students choose from a number of research areas, including biomolecular engineering; complex fluids; electronic materials; energy and sustainability; and polymer science. Research in these areas is supported by the department’s core strengths in thermodynamics, transport phenomena, and reaction engineering, all with a strong underpinning in applied mathematics. The field maintains and fosters many formal and informal ties with other departments and centers at Cornell, including the Cornell Center for Materials Research, the Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source, the Cornell NanoScale Science and Technology Facility, the Energy Institute, and the Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology.

Description:
Research in the graduate field of chemistry and chemical biology (C&CB) is organized into three main areas: physical chemistry, organic chemistry, and inorganic chemistry. Much of the research in the field, however, cuts across the traditional boundaries.

Sub-disciplines include analytical, bioorganic, biophysical, materials, organic synthesis, organometallic, physical organic, polymer, and theoretical chemistry.

An M.S. degree is offered for students who want a more in-depth background in chemistry than that provided by a bachelor’s degree, but who do not wish to commit to a Ph.D. program. The M.S. degree is generally completed in two years.

Description: Research in the graduate field of chemistry and chemical biology (C&CB) offers a wide range of opportunities in the chemical sciences. Research concentrations include analytical chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry, biophysical chemistry, chemical biology, inorganic chemistry, materials chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, and theoretical chemistry.
ScholarshipType: Research assistantships (RAs), teaching assistantships (TAs), graduate research assistantships (GRAs), and fellowships.

Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) in regional science is a non-professional degree intended to serve as an introduction to research and scholarship in planning. This program is not accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board. A research paper is required. It is a two-year program of study.
Accredidation: This program is not accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board.

Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Description: The graduate field of city and regional planning has a distinguished history of training students for professional careers and for research and teaching. The field is concerned with the processes of urbanization and with the art and science of city and regional planning—the analysis and design of human settlements and their environments. The field’s primary objective is to make human settlements better places in which to live. Students entering the field come from a wide variety of undergraduate programs, including architecture, business, economics, engineering, environmental studies, geography, government, history, international studies, political science, sociology, and urban studies. The field is made up of a wide-ranging, interdisciplinary group of faculty members.
ScholarshipAmount: Guaranteed funding for M.S. students includes a full tuition waiver, a living allowance stipend, and student health insurance.

Department: College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
Concentration: Built Environment, Development Studies, Historical Preservation Planning, International Studies in Planning, Regional Science, Urban and Regional Studies, Real Estate
Description:
The graduate field of city and regional planning has a long and distinguished history at Cornell. Its nationally recognized programs are part of the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. The field offers several graduate degrees: a professional Master of Regional Planning (M.R.P.) degree; a Master of Arts (M.A.) in regional science; a Master of Science (M.S.) in historic preservation; and a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in city and regional planning. In addition, the field offers a Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in real estate; a graduate minor in real estate; and an undergraduate degree in urban and regional studies.

Students come to the field from a wide variety of undergraduate disciplines and from throughout the United States and the world. Many have had several years of professional experience before entering the program.

Specializations for the Ph.D. degree correspond to the concentration offerings: Built Environment, Development Studies, Historic Preservation Planning, International Studies in Planning, Regional Science, and Urban and Regional Studies. Students also may design their own specialization. A separate concentration in real estate is available, administered through the Baker Program in Real Estate.

Department: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
Concentration: Civil and Environmental Engineering (general), Environmental Engineering, Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Hydrology, Environmental Processes, Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Systems Engineering
Description: The graduate field of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) has a long and distinguished history of providing a world-class graduate education that is at the forefront of the profession. We have a vibrant graduate program with approximately 170 M.S. and Ph.D. students working with 35 faculty members. CEE offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees that are flexible and that can be tailored to the specific interests of the student. CEE offers research-based M.S. and Ph.D. degrees, and a professional Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) degree. Graduate students in CEE conduct leading-edge research, are advised by our world-renowned faculty, and have access to world-class laboratory and computational facilities. Graduate research in CEE encompasses three strategic areas: Civil Infrastructure, Environment, and Systems Engineering and a variety of specialized concentrations. Current research efforts are focused on both fundamental and applied issues with a strong emphasis on innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Concentration: Civil and Environmental Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Hydrology, Environmental Processes, Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Systems Engineering
Description: The graduate field of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Cornell is a vibrant and diverse community of faculty members and graduate students whose interests span the full spectrum of the discipline. The field has two separate Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree programs located in Ithaca, NY, that emphasize research and advanced study. Students develop a program of study in one of a number of concentration areas. Coursework provides a strong background in the fundamentals of a chosen concentration, and M.S. and Ph.D. students work closely with a faculty advisor on a research topic that can range from fundamental to applied. Students are given the flexibility to construct an individualized course of study and research program tailored to their specific interests, and are given the opportunity to obtain a graduate minor in a wide range of related fields.

Concentration: ['Civil Engineering Materials', 'Environmental and Water Resources Systems Engineering', 'Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Hydrology', 'Environmental Processes', 'Geotechnical Engineering', 'Structural Engineering', 'Transportation Systems Engineering', 'Remote Sensing']
Description:
The graduate field of civil and environmental engineering has a long and distinguished history of providing a world-class graduate education. For more than one hundred years, the field has been a leader in teaching and research, and our graduates hold top positions in academic, government, and corporate institutions both nationally and internationally. The field offers Ph.D. and M.S. degrees, both of which require a student to specialize in one of eight major subject areas and to complete a thesis. In addition, the field also offers a professional Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) degree, which is a one-year, course-based program. The Master of Engineering degree program is separately administered by the College of Engineering. 

Research facilities are available in Bovay Laboratory, Hollister Hall, and Thurston Hall. The George Winter Laboratory for a new generation of large-scale, multi-hazard, testing of sustainable and resilient infrastructure systems, the DeFrees Hydraulics Laboratory, and the Center for Brownfield Studies facilities are available as well for research and teaching.

Concentration: ['Ancient History', 'Ancient Philosophy', 'Classical Archaeology', 'Classical Philology and Literature', 'Indo-European Linguistics']
Description:
The graduate field of Classics at Cornell has a long and distinguished tradition of training students for academic careers. The field offers Ph.D. degrees in five concentrations: Ancient History, Ancient Philosophy, Classical Archaeology, Classical Philology and Literature, and Indo-European Linguistics. Students are expected to complete the doctoral degree within five years.

The field combines a traditional emphasis on philological and literary training with the historical study of all aspects of the Greco-Roman world. The faculty has great strength in Greek and Latin philology, Greek and Roman history, classical art and archaeology, ancient philosophy, Greek and Roman religion, and Indo-European linguistics.

Students take advantage of formal and informal ties with several other fields and programs, including the graduate fields of History, Philosophy, and History of Art & Archaeology; the Cornell Institute of Archaeology and Material Studies (CIAMS); the Medieval Studies, Religious Studies, and Feminist, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Programs; and the Society for the Humanities. These ties make it possible to incorporate a broad range of interdisciplinary training into the curriculum.

The field also provides exceptional opportunities for professional development, including experience in teaching Latin, Greek, and other classics courses. There are numerous lecture series and colloquia at Cornell that bring in internationally-recognized scholars to speak on topics relevant to the field of Classics. Students regularly organize workshops and conferences to foster their own and their peers’ research interests and intellectual development. Resources for travel to conferences and for research are readily available from both the field and the Graduate School. In addition to a generous fellowship package that includes summer support, the field awards several prizes annually to graduate students for distinguished work in Latin, Greek, and other areas of classical studies.

Finally, the Cornell University Library is one of the world’s great research libraries.

Description:
The graduate field of cognitive science provides a unique Ph.D. program that takes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of mind and intelligence. The program is appropriate for students with interests that bridge traditional departmental boundaries and who wish to address questions that require the tools of several disciplines.

Students may choose one of five concentrations: Language and Cognition, Perception and Cognition, Cognition and Development, Computation and Cognition, and Neuroscience and Cognition. All students take several core courses and then develop a program tailored to their specific interests with the help of a Special Committee. Students choose a primary mentor from the field faculty, and two minor mentors, one of whom must be from a different discipline than the primary mentor. The Ph.D. in cognitive science is intended to prepare students for a career in academic research and teaching, or for a position in the growing number of commercial enterprises that rely on cognitive science research.

The graduate minor in cognitive science is available to any student in a regular graduate degree program at Cornell.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: ['communication and technology', 'risk and science communication', 'media communication']
Description: The graduate field of communication focuses on the study of communication as a social science. Students concentrate on one of the following areas: communication and technology, risk and science communication, or media communication. The graduate program emphasizes theory development and research. Research is broadly defined to include a wide array of quantitative and qualitative methods. All students are required to gain a thorough grounding in communication theory and research methods. Most research in communication is problem-oriented and draws from a variety of disciplines and theoretical perspectives. Faculty research covers topics in communication and technology, media communication, and risk and science communication. More specific research areas include digital media and society, human-computer interaction, group and organizational communication, media effects, media psychology, health communication, risk communication, science and environmental communication, and visual communication. The field has state-of-the-art research facilities, including a virtual reality lab, a social media lab, a human-robot interaction lab, a communication and collaborative technology lab, a survey research lab, a psychophysiology and media effects lab, and a health communication lab.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Media Communication; Science, Health, Environment, and Risk Communication; Communication and Technology
Description: The graduate field of communication at Cornell has a long and distinguished history. The field is committed to the study of communication as a social phenomenon. Faculty and students conduct research on a wide range of topics related to communication processes and effects, at levels from the individual to society as a whole. Doctoral students work closely with their Special Committee to develop a course of study appropriate to their area of interest. Research in the field can be grouped into three main areas of faculty research: (1) media communication; (2) science, health, environmental, and risk communication; and (3) communication and technology. The field’s unique strength is in the application of communication theory and research to compelling social problems. Research methodologies include both qualitative and quantitative approaches. Students have access to a state-of-the-art research facility, including a media effects laboratory. There is an active colloquium series. The graduate field is centered in the Department of Communication in the College of Agriculture and Llife Sciences.
ScholarshipType: Funding package (stipend, tuition waiver, health insurance)

Concentration: Development, Epigenetics and Genomics; Immunology and Infectious Disease; Molecular and Cellular Medicine; Neuroscience; Pharmacology; Stem Cell Biology; Translational Medicine; Systems and Computational Biology
Description: The graduate field of Comparative Biomedical Sciences (CBS) offers M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs to a diverse group of students with interests in the health of animals and humans. Research programs within the field of CBS are housed within the seven departments of the College of Veterinary Medicine and Baker Institute for Animal Health. More than 100 faculty members from the College of Veterinary Medicine, other colleges at Cornell, and the USDA serve as mentors for students in the field of CBS. The field embraces the philosophy of One Health, which is dedicated to improving the lives of all species through the integration of human medicine, veterinary medicine, and environmental science. A diversity of research interests and expertise of our faculty, combined with state-of-the-art facilities, provide an exceptional training environment for our graduate students. Research programs are available in eight concentrations: Development, Epigenetics and Genomics; Immunology and Infectious Disease; Molecular and Cellular Medicine; Neuroscience; Pharmacology; Stem Cell Biology; Translational Medicine and an interdisciplinary concentration in Systems and Computational Biology.

Concentration: Anesthesiology, Clinical Pathology, Comparative Biomedical Sciences, Diagnostic Imaging, Internal Medicine, Pharmacology, Physiology, Shelter Medicine, Surgery, Theriogenology, Zoological Medicine
Description: The graduate field of comparative biomedical sciences (CBS) provides interdisciplinary training in the basic and clinical sciences to prepare students for careers in academic research, government, or the private sector. Training opportunities are focused in five key areas: cancer biology, immunology and infectious disease, developmental and reproductive biology, musculoskeletal biology, and neuroscience. Students learn to conduct research in a collaborative environment and acquire strong communication and teaching skills. The program is designed to facilitate students’ successful transition to research-intensive careers, with an emphasis on research that stands at the interface of animal and human health.

Description: The field of comparative literature at Cornell has a long and distinguished history. It was one of the first in the country to be established as an independent department, and its faculty have included some of the most important figures in the field (e.g., Jonathan Culler, W. Wolfgang Holdheim, and Paul de Man). The graduate program encourages students to develop their own interests while ensuring that they have the broad competence in literary history and theory that the discipline requires. Students take courses in the Department of Literatures in English, German studies, romance studies, and the classics, as well as in other related fields in the humanities. All students are expected to take courses in literary theory.
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted Ph.D. students are offered five years of funding, including a stipend (the university minimum for 2024-2025 is $34,270), full tuition, and health insurance.

Concentration: Computational Biology, Computational Genetics and Genomics, Quantitative Methods in Systems Biology
Description: The graduate field of computational biology offers training in the development and application of data-analytical and theoretical methods, mathematical modeling, and computational simulation techniques to the study of biological systems. It is an interdisciplinary field, which brings together faculty from many different departments and programs to train a new generation of scientists. The program is flexible and students can design their coursework according to their specific interests.
ScholarshipType: Full funding for Ph.D. students (stipend, tuition, health insurance) through assistantships and fellowships.

Department: Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science
Concentration: ['Artificial Intelligence', 'Programming Languages and Logics', 'Scientific Computing and Applications', 'Systems', 'Theory of Computation', 'Computer Graphics', 'Computer Vision', 'Databases', 'Networks', 'Security', 'Robotics', 'Human Computer Interaction', 'Computational Science and Engineering', 'Machine Learning']
Description:
The Field of Computer Science has two separate graduate programs: a Ph.D. program and a terminal M.S. program. This page describes both programs. The Ph.D. program prepares students for a career in research and teaching. The M.S. program prepares students for a career in advanced development. It requires the completion of an independent project.

The Field of Computer Science is renowned for its research in the theory of computation, programming languages, artificial intelligence, and systems. More recently, the field has been building in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, and computational science and engineering. There are strong interdisciplinary ties with many other fields on campus, including Computational Biology, the Johnson Graduate School of Management, and the program in Cognitive Studies.

Department: Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science
Concentration: ['Artificial Intelligence', 'Computational Science and Engineering', 'Computer Graphics', 'Computer Science (general)', 'Network Science', 'Programming Languages and Logics', 'Robotics', 'Scientific Computing', 'Systems', 'Theory of Computation']
Description: The graduate field of computer science at Cornell is a large and diverse one, with faculty in all its major research areas. Many faculty members also are affiliated with other fields, so graduate students can draw upon related expertise in such areas as applied mathematics, cognitive studies, computational linguistics, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical engineering, and operations research.
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding package includes tuition, fees, and a stipend (9-month minimum stipend for 2024-25 is $43,136)
